title: No Time to Die
tagline: Some dinners are worth coming out of retirement for.
about: Bond is pulled out of retirement in Jamaica to rescue a kidnapped scientist.
cue: Serve the mains when Bond and Madeleine arrive at their hotel in the old town of Matera.

    StartersPaloma's Cuban party croquetasCreamy ham béchamel croquettes, crumbed and fried crispHow to make it60g butter70g plain flour, for the béchamel500ml milk, hot150g ham, finely choppednutmeg, a pinchsalt and pepper, to taste50g plain flour, for dusting2 eggs, beaten100g fine dried breadcrumbs1 L vegetable oil, for fryingMelt the butter, add the flour for the béchamel and cook for 3 minutes. Whisk in the hot milk a little at a time and cook, stirring, for 8 minutes until very thick.Stir in the ham, nutmeg, salt and pepper.Spread in a lined tray, press baking paper onto the surface and chill for at least 4 hours.With wet hands shape into 20 small logs.Roll in the flour for dusting, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.Heat the oil to 180°C in a deep heavy pan.Fry in batches for 2 to 3 minutes until deep golden, then drain.Serve hot.Port Antonio festival dumplingsLightly sweet Jamaican fried cornmeal dumplings, crisp outside and soft in the middleHow to make it200g plain flour100g fine cornmeal40g brown sugar2 tsp baking powder1/2 tsp salt200ml milk750ml vegetable oil, for fryingMix the flour, cornmeal, sugar, baking powder and salt.Stir in the milk, knead for 2 minutes to a firm smooth dough and rest for 10 minutes.Shape into 12 logs the length of a finger.Heat the oil to 170°C in a deep heavy pan.Fry in batches for about 6 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through.Drain and serve warm.MainsMatera orecchiette with broccolini and anchovyEar-shaped pasta tossed with broccolini, garlic, anchovy and chilli, pecorino and crunchy toasted breadcrumbsHow to make it60g fresh breadcrumbs80ml extra virgin olive oil400g dried orecchiette500g broccolini, cut into short lengths4 garlic cloves, sliced6 anchovy fillets1 tsp chilli flakes40g pecorino, grated1 lemon, zestedsalt, to tasteToast the breadcrumbs in 1 tbsp of the oil until golden and crisp. Set aside.Boil the orecchiette in well salted water for 8 minutes, adding the broccolini for the last 4.Meanwhile warm the rest of the oil with the garlic, anchovies and chilli on low heat, stirring, until the anchovies melt.Drain, keeping a cup of the pasta water. Toss the pasta and broccolini in the pan with a splash of the water, the pecorino and lemon zest until glossy.Serve topped with the toasted crumbs.Port Antonio jerk chicken with rice and peasBond's retirement in Jamaica, before Felix comes knockingHow to make it1kg chicken thighs, bone in4 spring onions1 Scotch bonnet or red chilli1 tsp ground allspice4 sprigs of thyme2 tbsp soy sauce1 lime300g long grain rice400ml coconut milk400g tin kidney beans, drained300g shredded cabbageBlitz the spring onion, chilli, allspice, thyme leaves, soy and lime juice and rub over the chicken.Grill or roast at 200°C until charred and cooked through.Simmer the rice with the coconut milk, beans, 250ml water and salt, covered, until tender.Serve with the shredded cabbage.SweetsMadeleine's Norway cardamom bunsTwisted Norwegian buns with cardamom dough, cinnamon butter and crunchy sugarHow to make it500g plain flour7g dried yeast80g caster sugar2 tsp ground cardamom1/2 tsp salt250ml milk, warmed2 eggs75g butter, softened, for the dough90g butter, softened, for the filling70g brown sugar1 tsp ground cinnamon2 tbsp pearl sugar or demeraraMix the flour, yeast, caster sugar, 1 tsp of the cardamom, salt, warm milk, 1 egg and the butter for the dough. Knead for 10 minutes until smooth and elastic.Cover and rise for an hour until doubled.Beat the butter for the filling with the brown sugar, cinnamon and the rest of the cardamom.Roll the dough to 40 x 30cm, spread with the filling, fold in thirds, cut into 12 strips and twist each into a knot. Lay on lined trays.Prove for 40 minutes until puffy, heating the oven to 200°C.Brush with the second egg, beaten, scatter with the pearl sugar and bake for 15 minutes until golden.Cool for 5 minutes before serving.DrinksPaloma's Santiago mojitoWhite rum, fresh lime, mint and sugar syrup over crushed ice, topped with sodaHow to make it1 bunch mint60ml sugar syrup3 limes3 cups crushed ice180ml white rum400ml soda water, chilledJuice 2 of the limes and cut the third into wedges.
